advances:
The transverse-support dichotomy is false under the complete
Alternative 1 hypotheses.  The two rational polygons below have all
eight prescribed cell areas and satisfy the strict high-high
mixed-area constraint, but after full-trace normalization their
positive \(A_0\) cell has unique rightmost and topmost points with
both transverse inequalities reversed.
author: mp_r104_regime_a_transverse_support
proof:
First verify convexity.  For the listed cyclic vertices of \(A_0\),
the successive edge cross products, at
\(E_0,R_0,T_0,F_0,N_0,L_0\), respectively, are
\[
\frac{505763}{698400},\quad
\frac{97}{450},\quad
\frac{97}{450},\quad
\frac{73051}{100800},\quad
\frac{117}{1940},\quad
\frac{117}{1960}.
\]
For the listed cyclic vertices of \(A_2\), the corresponding cross
products at \(E_2,R_2,T_2,F_2,C_2,S_2,D_2\) are
\[
\frac{107}{3200},\quad
\frac1{100},\quad
\frac1{100},\quad
\frac{107}{3200},\quad
\frac3{2000},\quad
\frac{39}{6400},\quad
\frac3{2000}.
\]
They are all positive, so both displayed hulls are two-dimensional
convex polygons with exactly the stated cyclic boundaries.

Let
\[
Q_0=\operatorname{conv}
\{(0,0),E_2,R_2,T_2,F_2\}.
\]
Shoelace gives
\[
|Q_0|
=\frac12\left(\frac7{200}+\frac1{50}+\frac7{200}\right)
=\frac9{200}.
\]
The segment \(N_0L_0\) lies on \(y=-x\) and passes through the
origin.  Hence
\[
P=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),E_0,R_0,T_0,F_0\}.
\]
In fact
\[
P=
\begin{pmatrix}97/21&0\\0&14/3\end{pmatrix}Q_0,
\qquad
\det
\begin{pmatrix}97/21&0\\0&14/3\end{pmatrix}
=\frac{194}{9}.
\]
Therefore
\[
|P|=\frac{194}{9}\frac9{200}=\frac{97}{100}.
\]
The remaining \(A_0\) cells are the triangles
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),F_0,N_0\},\qquad
\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),L_0,E_0\},
\]
and the southwest cell has area zero.  Their areas are
\[
\frac12\frac{14}{15}\frac9{280}=\frac3{200},
\qquad
\frac12\frac{97}{105}\frac{63}{1940}=\frac3{200}.
\]
This proves the entire \(A_0\) row.

For \(A_2\), its four quadrant cells are
\[
Q_0,\quad
\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),F_2,C_2\},\quad
\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),D_2,E_2\},\quad
\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),C_2,S_2,D_2\}.
\]
The two mixed triangles both have area
\[
\frac12\frac15\frac1{16}=\frac1{160}.
\]
The two nonzero determinant contributions to the southwest
quadrilateral are both \(1/200\), so its area is
\[
\frac12\left(\frac1{200}+\frac1{200}\right)=\frac1{200}.
\]
Together with \(|Q_0|=9/200\), this proves the entire \(A_2\) row,
including all three prescribed nonpositive cells.

It remains to verify the strict high-high constraint exactly.  Merge
the cyclic edge lists of \(P\) and \(Q=Q_0\).  The three nontrivial
edge-order comparisons reduce to
\[
7<\frac{686}{97},\qquad
1<\frac{98}{97},\qquad
\frac17<\frac{14}{97}.
\]
Thus \(P+Q\) has the following counterclockwise vertex list:
\[
\begin{gathered}
(0,0),\ (118/105,0),\ (193/168,7/40),\
(177/140,119/120),\\
(31/30,49/40),\ (59/60,51/40),\
(97/120,5/4),\ (0,17/15).
\end{gathered}
\]
Another shoelace calculation gives
\[
|P+Q|=\frac{2293}{1600}
=\frac{29}{20}-\frac{27}{1600}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\left|\frac{P+Q}{2}\right|
=\frac{2293}{6400}
=\frac{29}{80}-\frac{27}{6400}
<\frac{29}{80}.
\]

The full positive axis traces of \(P\) are
\[
[0,97/105]\times\{0\},\qquad
\{0\}\times[0,14/15].
\]
Apply the positive diagonal normalization
\[
(x,y)\longmapsto\left(\frac{105}{97}x,\frac{15}{14}y\right).
\]
It sends \(P\) to
\[
\widehat P=\operatorname{conv}
\{(0,0),(1,0),(9/8,7/8),(7/8,9/8),(0,1)\}.
\]
The point \((9/8,7/8)\) is its unique rightmost point and
\((7/8,9/8)\) is its unique topmost point.  Therefore
\((9/8,9/8)\notin\widehat P\), while the only possible support-point
choices have
\[
X=Y=\frac78<1=A=B.
\]
This is the asserted failure of both alternatives in the
transverse-support dichotomy.

All hypotheses of accepted fact `92a1b537d7e7876c` have now been
checked for this same pair \(P,Q\), so its translated inner and outer
homothetic containments also hold.  Maximizing the inner scale and
minimizing the outer scale over translations gives contact homothets,
with attainment by compactness of these polygons.  Hence the bad
support order coexists not only with the full \(A_2\) extension and
the strict high-high bound, but also with the available
homothetic/contact information.
statement:
Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
L_0&=(63/1940,-63/1940),&
E_0&=(97/105,0),\\
R_0&=(291/280,49/60),&
T_0&=(97/120,21/20),\\
F_0&=(0,14/15),&
N_0&=(-9/280,9/280),
\end{aligned}
\]
and define the rational polygon
\[
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{L_0,E_0,R_0,T_0,F_0,N_0\},
\]
where the vertices are in counterclockwise order.  Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_2&=(0,-1/16),&
E_2&=(1/5,0),\\
R_2&=(9/40,7/40),&
T_2&=(7/40,9/40),\\
F_2&=(0,1/5),&
C_2&=(-1/16,0),\\
S_2&=(-2/25,-2/25),
\end{aligned}
\]
and define the rational polygon
\[
A_2=\operatorname{conv}
\{D_2,E_2,R_2,T_2,F_2,C_2,S_2\},
\]
again in counterclockwise order.  With quadrant boundaries ignored
as null sets, these polygons satisfy
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
&(+,+)&(-,+)&(+,-)&(-,-)\\ \hline
A_0&97/100&3/200&3/200&0\\
A_2&9/200&1/160&1/160&1/200.
\end{array}
\]
If
\[
P=A_0\cap\{x\geq0,y\geq0\},\qquad
Q=A_2\cap\{x\geq0,y\geq0\},
\]
then
\[
\left|\frac{P+Q}{2}\right|=\frac{2293}{6400}
<\frac{29}{80}.
\]
Nevertheless, after normalizing the two full positive axis traces of
\(P\) to unit length, one has
\[
(W,H)\notin P,
\]
and the unique rightmost and topmost points are
\[
R=(W,Y)=(9/8,7/8),\qquad
T=(X,H)=(7/8,9/8).
\]
Thus \(A=B=1\) but \(X<A\) and \(Y<B\).
